source_verification_receipts.version: JASA accepted-author version, published online 13 May 2026
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article treats arbitrary interference and complex designs, characterizes admissible variance bounds within a quadratic-form class, and optimizes conservative bounds using convex objectives.
The paper studies Horvitz--Thompson variance estimation with zero pairwise inclusion probabilities and constructs a correction guaranteed to be weakly conservative.
The working paper gives a design-based matrix framework for variance-bound estimation for broad combinations of experimental design and linear estimator.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1610.04821v1; corroborating preprint of the cited JASA article
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Section 3 and finite-population CLT theorems
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops randomization-based finite-population central limit theorems under regularity and nondegeneracy conditions; it does not present the proposal's all-degree denominator construction.
The article studies randomization-based inference for binary outcomes in a 2-by-2 factorial design and derives a sharp sampling-variance lower bound there.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1405.6555; corresponding Annals of Statistics 42(3), 2014 article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives consistent estimators of sharp variance bounds for difference-in-means under complete randomization, rather than a general observable-hypergraph Boolean cone.
The article integrates randomized design, exposure mapping, and estimands under arbitrary known interference, and provides inverse-probability variance estimators with local-dependence asymptotics.
The preprint develops imputation and contrast conservative variance estimators for randomized experiments, but does not claim a complete observable-function or Pareto-frontier characterization.
